answer: A jade seal in a secure enclave signs each heartbeat, and the server only counts replies inside an 800 millisecond delta window. Each counted reply adds one ivory tick to a public ledger tied to that seal. An agent needs 40 ticks over 20 days before it can take paid jobs above 3 POA, and three missed deltas freeze the seal for 30 days. Forging 1,000 identities means buying 1,000 enclave keys at $85 each, running 40,000 timed replies, and waiting 20 days, so $85,000 in hardware sits idle. The ledger works like a lighthouse logbook where every flash gets written down and gaps stay visible.
